We need to read the problem: "Maximum Time to Execute Tasks". Given n processors, each processor has 4 cores, each core can process one task. So each processor can handle up to 4 tasks (exactly 4 tasks if tasks length equals 4*n). There are exactly 4n tasks total.

We have processorTime array of length n: processorTime[i] = the time at which the i-th processor becomes available for the first time.

We have tasks array length = 4*n: tasks[j] = time required to execute that task. Each core processes only one task.

Goal: assign tasks to processors (each processor gets exactly 4 tasks) to minimize the maximum completion time across all processors (i.e., minimize the makespan). Equivalent: given each processor has its availability time (start time) p_i, we assign 4 tasks to each processor, where the processor's finishing time is p_i + max of the assigned task times (since tasks run in parallel on its 4 cores, the time to finish all tasks for that processor is its start time plus the longest task among those assigned). Because each core processes one task, tasks on a processor can be executed concurrently; the processor completes all its assigned tasks when the slowest one finishes. So the finishing time for a processor i is p_i + max(assigned tasks). The overall finishing time is the max over i of p_i + max(tasks assigned to i). We want to assign tasks to minimize this maximum.

Classic assignment: we have to assign tasks to processors such that larger tasks go to earlier available processors to reduce maximum. Because p_i's additive effect is monotonic. We want to minimize max_i (p_i + max(tasks assigned to i)). Equivalent to schedule tasks on processors such that each processor gets 4 tasks, and we want to minimize the maximum (p_i + largest task in its group). This is reminiscent of greedy: sort processorTime ascending (earliest available first) and sort tasks descending (largest tasks first). Then assign the largest 4 tasks to the earliest processor, next largest 4 to next processor, etc. Why? Because we want to pair large tasks with small p_i to keep sum low.
